chapter: Russell and Armstrong years, Goodman and the road
title: Listening to West End Blues
summary: They play West End Blues; he identifies Luis Russell's band, and Red Allen and Russell on the record.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yeah, well, that's why we were talking about the Luis Russell period because like I know he recorded a lot of songs and I didn't know some of the songs were your songs. I know there was a period when you came with the band, with Luis Russell's band or with Louis Armstrong's band, you were with Luis Russell's band and then Louis Armstrong came in front of the band.
Well, what I wanted to ask you about was some of the musicians that were in that band when some of those things were recorded like West End Blues, you mentioned By and By.
You know the West End Blues?
That's the way I practice at home -- good exercise.
How's that, the doo, da, doo, la, loo?
Oh, yeah. When you get to (.?)
Because I have West End Blues here, have you heard it lately?
... (inaudible) (plays the record) (comments during the record inaudible but refer to JCH's solo) ...
That's Louis Armstrong's trumpet, Red Allen back there.
And the solo you take on this is fantastic. You remember that solo?
How did the people do for this when y'all played this in person?
